f.title: Submit a PSUR for all approved medicinal products in the UK, irrespective of marketing status
f.statement: The MAH must submit a periodic safety update report (PSUR) for all approved medicinal products in the UK, unless they are covered by the derogation given in the Human Medicines Regulations 2012, as amended. This must be done irrespective of the marketing status of the product (whether it is placed on the market or not).
f.applicability: All medicinal products approved in the UK, whether or not placed on the market
f.exceptions: Products covered by the derogation given in the Human Medicines Regulations 2012, as amended

rows.quote:
You must submit a periodic safety update report (PSUR) for all approved medicinal products in the UK (unless they are covered by the derogation given in the Human Medicines Regulations 2012, as amended).

 The PSUR is a periodic assessment of the risk-benefit balance of the product. You need to do this irrespective of the marketing status of the product (whether it is placed on the market or not).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: 'You must submit' proves the main duty; the 'irrespective of marketing status' part rests on 'You need to do this', read as Mandatory (judgement call), so held below 90.

f.title: Include information on new limitations of the medicine and alternative treatment areas in the PSUR
f.statement: Although most PSUR information will likely relate to safety, the MAH should include information on any new limitations of the medicine and alternative treatment areas.

rows.quote: Most information will likely be related to safety, but you should include information on any new limitations of the medicine and alternative treatment areas.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed; 'should' = Recommended, quote proves the statement.

f.title: Do not wait for the PSUR to notify the MHRA of significant new safety and efficacy information
f.statement: The MAH must not wait for the PSUR submission to notify the MHRA of significant new information relating to the safety and efficacy of its product.

rows.quote: You must not wait for the PSUR submission to notify us of significant new information relating to the safety and efficacy of your product.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed; 'must not' = Mandatory.

f.title: Send standalone signal notifications to the MHRA in line with GVP IX
f.statement: In line with GVP IX requirements, standalone notifications of signals should be sent to the MHRA.

rows.quote: In line with GVP IX requirements, standalone notifications of signals should be sent to the MHRA
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: removed '(to the MHRA signal management mailbox)' from the statement because the quote stops before the address and does not prove it. Below 90: passive 'should be sent' leaves the actor (MAH) inferred.

f.title: Notify the MHRA in writing of an emerging safety issue
f.statement: When a MAH becomes aware of an emerging safety issue, it should notify it in writing to the MHRA.

rows.deadline: On becoming aware of the emerging safety issue (no time frame stated)
rows.quote: When a MAH becomes aware of an emerging safety issue, they should notify it in writing to the MHRA
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: removed the mailbox parenthetical (not in the quote); 'should' and MAH actor are explicit.

f.title: Follow the standard PSUR submission cycle after grant of a UK marketing authorisation
f.statement: If the MAH has just been granted a UK Marketing Authorisation it usually needs to submit its PSUR every 6 months until the product is placed on the market, every 6 months for the first 2 years after the product is placed on the market, and once a year for the following 2 years.
f.exceptions: Overridden by the EURD list submission date for the active substance, and may differ where specific conditions were given with the MA (see related rows)

rows.deadline: Every 6 months until the product is placed on the market; every 6 months for the first 2 years after placing on the market; once a year for the following 2 years
rows.quote:
If you have just been granted a UK Marketing Authorisation ( MA ) you usually need to submit your PSUR:

 every 6 months until the product is placed on the market

 every 6 months for the first 2 years after the product is placed on the market

 once a year for the following 2 years
rows.review_note: Review: kept Mandatory: 'need to submit' read as binding, consistent with the committed MHRA QPPV/PSMF curation ('needs to be' = Mandatory); statement keeps the source's 'usually', and the EURD list override and MA-specific conditions stay in exceptions. Double-check: Mandatory rests on 'usually need to', a hedged judgement-call level; the cycle is also overridden by the EURD list, so below 90.

f.title: Check the EURD list for the PSUR submission date, which overrides the general cycle
f.statement: At least initially the UK will continue to follow the European reference date (EURD) list, so the MAH should check it for the exact submission date relating to the active substance in its product; this overrides the general cycle. The cycle may also be different if specific conditions were given when the MA was applied for.
f.exceptions: The cycle may differ where specific conditions were given with the MA

rows.deadline: Exact submission date per the EURD list for the active substance
rows.quote: At least initially the UK will continue to follow the European reference date (EURD) list so check this for the exact submission date relating to the active substance in your product, which overrides the general cycle above. The cycle may also be different if you were given specific conditions when you applied for your MA .
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: level Recommended for the bare imperative 'check this' is a judgement call, so below 90.

f.title: MHRA may request a PSUR outside the set deadlines where appropriate
f.statement: Although PSUR deadlines have been set, the MHRA may request a PSUR where appropriate.

rows.quote: Although these deadlines have been set, MHRA may request a PSUR at where appropriate.
rows.review_note: Review: title and actor narrowed to the MHRA's permission to request a PSUR (the source states no MAH deadline for responding); added submissions-2 (authority liaison) as consulted. Typo 'at where' kept verbatim. Double-check: authority-only row (MHRA permission); quote has a source typo ('at where'); below 90.

f.title: Make a separate UK submission for PSURs with a submission deadline after 1 January 2021
f.statement: Any PSUR for a UK MA with a submission deadline after 1 January 2021 will require a separate submission to the UK.
f.applicability: PSURs for UK MAs with a submission deadline after 1 January 2021

rows.quote: Any PSUR, for a UK MA , with a submission deadline after 1 January 2021 will require a separate submission to the UK.
rows.review_note: Review: kept Mandatory: 'will require a separate submission' is a binding consequence, consistent with the committed MHRA QPPV/PSMF curation ('will require you to make a resubmission' = Mandatory). Double-check: Mandatory from 'will require a separate submission' (no must) is a judgement-call level; actor inferred from the passive wording; below 90.

f.title: Submit the EU version of the PSUR with a UK-specific annex where needed
f.statement: The EU versions of the PSUR can be submitted, but where the UK has made a specific request for information or where there is UK-specific information relevant to the benefit/risk assessment, this should be included in a specific annex. How this is presented will depend on the nature of the data; no specific template is available at this time.
f.applicability: UK-specific information requests and UK-specific benefit/risk information

rows.quote: The EU versions of the PSUR can be submitted, but where the UK has made a specific request for information or where there is UK-specific information relevant to the benefit/ risk assessment this should be included in a specific annex. How this is presented will depend upon the nature of the data to be included. A specific template is not available at this time.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Kept as one row: the permission to submit the EU version and the expectation of a UK-specific annex are one conditional duty. Double-check: mixed 'can'/'should be included' in passive voice; actor inferred; kept as one row; below 90.

f.title: Follow the standard PSUR cycle if the active substance is not on the EURD list
f.statement: If the MAH cannot find the submission date for its active substance on the EURD list, the standard PSUR cycle should be followed.
f.applicability: Active substances not on the EURD list

rows.quote: If you cannot find the submission date for your active substance on the EURD list the standard PSUR cycle should be followed.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed; 'should' = Recommended, condition addressed to 'you'.

f.title: Submit the PSUR within 70 or 90 days of the data lock point when not on the EURD list
f.statement: The specific submission date is based on the data lock point (DLP), the cut-off point for preparing the report (the end of the cycle). If the submission date is not on the EURD list, it will be 70 days after the DLP if the PSUR covers a period of 12 months or less, and 90 days after the DLP if the PSUR covers a period of 12 months or more.
f.applicability: Submission dates not on the EURD list

rows.deadline: 70 days after the DLP if the PSUR covers a period of 12 months or less; 90 days after the DLP if the PSUR covers a period of 12 months or more
rows.quote:
Your specific submission date is based on your ‘data lock point’ which is the cut off point for preparing your report (the end of the cycle). If your submission date is not on the EURD list, it will be:

 70 days after your DLP if your PSUR covers a period of 12 months or less

 90 days after your DLP if your PSUR covers a period of 12 months or more
rows.review_note: Review: kept Mandatory: the source fixes the default deadline ('it will be'), consistent with the committed MHRA QPPV/PSMF curation of binding 'will' statements. Kept the source's '12 months or less' / '12 months or more' wording exactly; note the source overlaps at exactly 12 months (both 70 and 90 days could apply) and does not resolve it. Clock start is the DLP; applies only where the submission date is not on the EURD list. Double-check: Mandatory from 'it will be' (no must) is a judgement call, and the source overlaps at exactly 12 months (both 70 and 90 days stated, unresolved); below 90.

f.title: Reuse DSUR and RMP modules in the PSUR to minimise duplication
f.statement: The MAH may be able to use some of the same modules in the development safety update report (DSUR) and/or risk management plan in the PSUR to minimise duplication and improve efficiency (see appendix D in the ICH guidelines).

rows.quote: You may be able to use some of the same modules in the development safety update report (DSUR) and or risk management plan in the PSUR to minimise duplication and improve efficiency. See appendix D in the ICH guidelines for more information.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed; 'may be able to' = Permitted.

f.title: Submit PSURs through the PSUR portal in MHRA Submissions
f.statement: PSURs should be submitted through the PSUR portal using MHRA Submissions. Access to MHRA Submissions can be given by a company administrator in the organisation.

rows.quote: PSURs should be submitted through PSUR portal using MHRA Submissions . You can be given access to MHRA Submissions by a company administrator in your organisation.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. The second sentence (access via a company administrator) is kept as context, not a separate duty. Double-check: 'PSURs should be submitted' is passive, so the actor is inferred; access sentence kept as context; below 90.

f.title: Submit one PSUR per active substance or combination per the EURD list
f.statement: The MAH should continue to submit one PSUR covering its medicinal products with the same active substance or combination of active substances according to the EURD list. It should include all authorised indications, routes of administration, and dosage forms and dosing regimens. This applies even if the products have different names.

rows.quote:
You should continue to submit one PSUR covering your medicinal products with the same active substance or combination of active substances according to the EURD list. This should include all:

 authorised indications

 routes of administration

 dosage forms and dosing regiments

 This applies even if the products have different names.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Source typo 'dosing regiments' kept verbatim in the quote; statement uses 'dosing regimens'. Double-check: confirmed; quote includes the bulleted list verbatim (source typo 'regiments' kept).

f.title: Submit separate PSURs for products with the same active substance only if agreed at MA grant
f.statement: The MAH should only submit separate PSURs for different products with the same active substance if this was agreed when the MA was granted, for example when there are different formulations of the active substance with significantly different indications.

rows.quote: You should only submit separate PSURs for different products with the same active substance if this was agreed when your MA was granted. For example when there are different formulations of the active substance with significantly different indications.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed; 'should only' = Recommended.

f.title: Prepare the PSUR following the ICH guidelines and GVP Module VII
f.statement: The MAH should follow the ICH guidelines and the Good pharmacovigilance guidelines (GVP VII) to prepare its PSUR.

rows.quote: You should follow the ICH guidelines and the Good pharmacovigilance guidelines (GVP VII) to prepare your PSUR.
rows.review_note: Review: statement corrected to the source's 'Good pharmacovigilance guidelines (GVP VII)' (was 'Good pharmacovigilance practice guidelines'). Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Critically examine new information for new signals and risks in the PSUR
f.statement: The PSUR should critically examine information received since the last PSUR to see if there are new signals that have led to potential or current risks, or update information on previous risks.
f.applicability: Content of the PSUR: one of the five items under the lead-in 'The PSUR should:' (Risk-benefit evaluations)

rows.quote:
The PSUR should:

 critically examine information received since your last PSUR to see if there are new signals that have led to potential or current risks or update information on previous risks
rows.review_note: Review: kept as a separate row for this 'The PSUR should:' bullet; lead-in recorded in applicability so the Recommended level is traceable. Double-check: lead-in 'The PSUR should:' is in the quote, but the actor (MAH) is inferred from a document as subject; below 90.

f.title: Summarise new information that could affect the risk-benefit balance in the PSUR
f.statement: The PSUR should summarise any new information on the safety, efficacy and effectiveness of the product that could affect its risk-benefit balance.
f.applicability: Content of the PSUR: one of the five items under the lead-in 'The PSUR should:' (Risk-benefit evaluations)

rows.quote: summarise any new information on the safety, efficacy and effectiveness of the product that could affect its risk-benefit balance

f.title: Provide an integrated benefit-risk analysis for all authorised indications in the PSUR
f.statement: The PSUR should provide an integrated benefit-risk analysis from the date of an interventional clinical trial (in any country) for all authorised indications; if the date is not known or the information cannot be accessed, the earliest applicable date for clinical developments should be used as a starting point.
f.applicability: Content of the PSUR: one of the five items under the lead-in 'The PSUR should:' (Risk-benefit evaluations)
f.exceptions: If the date is unknown or the information cannot be accessed, use the earliest applicable date for clinical developments as the starting point

rows.quote: provide an integrated benefit-risk analysis from the date of an interventional clinical trial (in any country) for all authorised indications - if you don’t know the date or you can’t access the information use the earliest applicable date for clinical developments as a starting point
rows.review_note: Review: kept as a separate row for this 'The PSUR should:' bullet; lead-in recorded in applicability so the Recommended level is traceable. Double-check: level taken from the lead-in 'The PSUR should:' recorded in applicability, not in the quote; actor inferred; below 90.

f.title: Summarise risk minimisation actions implemented or planned during the reporting interval
f.statement: The PSUR should summarise any risk minimisation actions implemented or planned during the reporting interval.
f.applicability: Content of the PSUR: one of the five items under the lead-in 'The PSUR should:' (Risk-benefit evaluations)

rows.quote: summarise any risk minimisation actions implemented or planned during the reporting interval

f.statement: The PSUR should outline plans for signal or risk evaluations including timelines and/or proposals for additional pharmacovigilance activities.
f.applicability: Content of the PSUR: one of the five items under the lead-in 'The PSUR should:' (Risk-benefit evaluations)

f.title: Include results of new safety studies on off-label use in the PSUR
f.statement: The MAH should also include in the PSUR the results of any new studies carried out on the safety of its product around off-label use, with a summary of their impact.

rows.quote: You should also include the results of any new studies carried out on the safety of your product around off-label use, with a summary of their impact.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed; 'should also include' = Recommended.

f.title: Include the sources of efficacy, effectiveness and safety information in the risk-benefit evaluation
f.statement: To help demonstrate efficacy, effectiveness and safety in the risk-benefit evaluation the MAH needs to include sources. These may include non-clinical studies; spontaneous reports (e.g. reports on the MAH safety database); active surveillance systems (e.g. sentinel sites); investigations of product quality; product usage data and drug utilisation information; clinical trials, including research in unauthorised indications or populations; observational studies, including registries; patient support programs; systematic reviews and meta-analysis; MAH-sponsored websites; published scientific literature or reports from abstracts, including information presented at scientific meetings; unpublished manuscripts; licensing partners, other sponsors or academic institutions and research networks; and competent authorities (worldwide).
f.clause: Efficacy, effectiveness and safety information of the product

rows.quote:
To help demonstrate this in your risk-benefit evaluation you need to include sources. These may include:

 non-clinical studies

 spontaneous reports (for example, reports on the marketing authorisation holder’s safety database)

 active surveillance systems (for example, sentinel sites)

 investigations of product quality

 product usage data and drug utilisation information

 clinical trials, including research in unauthorised indications or populations

 observational studies, including registries

 patient support programs

 systematic reviews and meta-analysis

 marketing authorisation holders’ sponsored websites

 published scientific literature or reports from abstracts, including information presented at scientific meetings

 unpublished manuscripts

 licensing partners, other sponsors or academic institutions and research networks

 competent authorities (worldwide)
rows.location: Efficacy, effectiveness and safety information of the product
rows.review_note: Review: kept Mandatory: 'you need to include sources' read as binding, consistent with the committed MHRA QPPV/PSMF curation ('needs to be' = Mandatory); the listed sources stay permissive ('These may include'). Double-check: Mandatory rests on 'you need to include sources' (no must), a judgement-call level; list items are permissive ('may include'); below 90.

f.title: Include other sources of information in the PSUR where they demonstrate risks and benefits
f.statement: The MAH can include sources other than those listed to demonstrate the risks and benefits of the medicinal product.
f.clause: Efficacy, effectiveness and safety information of the product

rows.quote: You can include other sources outside of those above to demonstrate the risks and benefits of the medicinal product.
rows.location: Efficacy, effectiveness and safety information of the product
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed; 'can' = Permitted.

f.title: No routine PSURs for generic, well-established use, homeopathic and traditional herbal products
f.statement: The MAH does not need to submit routine PSURs if its medicinal product falls under article 10.1 (generic, previously article 10.1 a ii), article 10.a (well established use, previously article 4.8ii), article 14 (homeopathic medicine) or article 16a (traditional herbal medicine) of Directive 2001/83/EC, unless there is a specific condition in the MA or it is indicated in the EURD list.
f.applicability: Products authorised under Directive 2001/83/EC article 10.1, 10.a, 14 or 16a
f.exceptions: Routine PSURs are still required where there is a specific condition in the MA or it is indicated in the EURD list

rows.quote:
You do not need to submit routine PSURs if your medicinal product falls under some articles in the European Commission’s directive (2001/83/EC), unless there’s a specific condition in your MA or it’s indicated in the EURD list. These are:

 article 10.1 generic (previously article 10.1 a ii)

 article 10.a - well established use (previously article 4.8ii)

 article 14 - homeopathic medicine

 article 16a - traditional herbal medicine
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: exemption ('do not need to') recorded as Permitted is a judgement-call level; statement and conditions match the quote; below 90.

f.title: Pay the fee for PSUR assessment for actives or combinations on the EURD list or future UKRD
f.statement: A fee will be payable for the assessment of PSURs for actives/combinations currently listed on the EURD or future UKRD. There will be a reduction in fee for each PSUR where more than one Marketing Authorisation Holder is involved in the procedure.
f.applicability: PSURs for actives/combinations listed on the EURD list or future UKRD
f.exceptions: Reduced fee for each PSUR where more than one MAH is involved in the procedure

rows.quote: A fee will be payable for the assessment of PSURs for actives/ combinations currently listed on the EURD or future UKRD. There will be a reduction in fee for each PSUR where more than one Marketing Authorisation Holder is involved in the procedure.
rows.review_note: Review: kept Mandatory: 'A fee will be payable' is a binding fee obligation, consistent with the committed MHRA QPPV/PSMF curation of binding 'will' statements (fee in 0044); fee reduction for multi-MAH procedures kept in exceptions. Double-check: Mandatory from 'will be payable' (no must) is a judgement-call level; payer (MAH) inferred; below 90.

f.title: Amend product information after PSUR assessment by Type IA variation (no further fee)
f.statement: Following PSUR assessment, no further fee will be payable for the amendment of the product information as a result of the assessment; the updates will be made by a Type IA variation.
f.applicability: Product information amendments resulting from a PSUR assessment

rows.quote: No further fee will be payable for the amendment of the product information as a result of the assessment, updates will be made by a Type IA variation.

Double-check: Mandatory from 'updates will be made by a Type IA variation' (no must, passive) is a judgement-call level and the actor is inferred; partly a fee statement rather than a duty; below 90.
